title: GOOD: stoa-auth as consolidation target, not a new crate
description:
## What

The refactor consolidated the duplicate CredentialStore and UserCredential into stoa-auth (the existing crate at crates/auth), rather than creating a new crate (stoa-secrets, stoa-config-common) or merging the code into stoa-core.

## Why good

stoa-auth already existed, already depended on bcrypt, and already had the better-tested CredentialStore implementation with `is_empty()`, timing-safe dummy hash, and file-load variants. Using it as the consolidation target required zero new crates, zero new dependency edges, and zero changes to the 5+ non-reader crates that already imported from it.

Creating a new crate (the alternative listed in the epic description) would have required: new Cargo.toml, new workspace member, updating dependency declarations in every consumer, deciding where to draw the boundary, and a second round of review. It solves no problem that stoa-auth doesn't already solve.

Merging into stoa-core would have pulled bcrypt (a slow, specialized dep) into core, which is supposed to be a lean shared-types crate used by everything including embedded or constrained builds.

## Alternative avoided

New stoa-secrets or stoa-config-common crate: more churn, no benefit over the existing stoa-auth home. Merging into stoa-core: bloats core with an auth-specific dependency (bcrypt).
